query_text: first satellite compared to the latest

action.query: latest satellite launch June 2026 satellite launched
queries: latest satellite launch June 2026 satellite launched

content.text:
Assuming you mean **the first artificial satellite vs modern/latest satellites**:

| Feature | **First satellite: Sputnik 1** | **Modern/latest satellites** |
|---|---:|---:|
| Launch date | **October 4, 1957** | Ongoing — new satellites launch almost weekly/daily |
| Country/operator | Soviet Union | Many countries + private companies |
| Mass | About **83.6 kg** | From tiny **CubeSats** under 10 kg to large satellites several tons |
| Size | Metal sphere, **58 cm** wide | From shoebox-sized to bus-sized |
| Power | Batteries only | Solar panels + rechargeable batteries |
| Mission | Send simple radio “beeps” | Internet, GPS/navigation, weather, Earth imaging, science, defense, communications |
| Instruments | Radio transmitter + basic sensors | Cameras, radar, lasers, AI computers, advanced antennas, propulsion |
| Lifetime | About **3 weeks transmitting**; burned up after ~3 months | Months to **15+ years**, depending on design |
| Communication | Simple radio signal | High-speed data links, laser communications, broadband internet |
| Control | Very limited | Highly controlled, maneuverable, sometimes autonomous |
| Example of latest type | — | Starlink, Amazon Leo/Kuiper, Earth-observation radar satellites, GPS, climate satellites |

**In short:** Sputnik 1 was basically a simple radio beacon proving that humans could put an object in orbit. Modern satellites are advanced robotic spacecraft that can provide internet, guide phones and aircraft, monitor climate, image Earth in detail, and communicate huge amounts of data.

A recent example of modern satellites: SpaceX listed a **Starlink mission on June 8, 2026**, and China launched a new commercial satellite group on **June 4, 2026**. ([spacex.com](https://www.spacex.com/launches/sl-6-96?utm_source=openai))
